candidate.html:
Ohm's Law Simulator

Controls
Readout
2.00 A

Current I = V / R. Raising voltage raises current linearly; raising resistance lowers it. The line shows I vs V for the chosen resistance; the dot marks the current state.

contract.objective: Compare the effects of voltage and resistance on current through an ideal resistor.

visualVerdict.explanation: Screenshot 1 (V=12,R=1): line reaches I=12 at V=12, dot at (12,12), readout 12.00 A, circuit shows 1Ω/12V, I=12.00 A. Screenshot 2 (V=6,R=3): line slope 1/3 reaching 4 at V=12, dot at (6,2), readout 2.00 A, circuit 3Ω/6V, I=2.00 A. Axes correctly labeled Voltage(V) 0–12 and Current(A) 0–12, matching scale. Circuit topology forms a closed loop: source, wires, resistor, back to source; current arrow present with nonzero current, no gaps. Units outside readout. All values match Ohm's law. Correct teaching.
